title: Introduce KMS consent backoff, residency violation mitigator, and RBAC v2 operator fence
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add KMS consent backoff strategy, introduce residency-violation mitigation path with non-blocking audit, and enforce operator-scoped RBAC v2 fence for region-sensitive actions.
description:
Motivation: Some customers operating under stricter residency constraints saw transient KMS consent failures surface as hard rejects that returned 5xx to callers and triggered application-level incidents. This PR introduces a layered mitigation: a KMS consent backoff/retry policy with exponential jitter; a residency-violation mitigator that turns unexpected consent failures into controlled fallbacks (non-blocking mode + enriched audit events); and an Operator Fence enforcement in RBAC v2 so operator-scoped actions that might change residency-related configuration require an explicit operator scope assertion.

What this changes (high level):
- service/kms: add consent_backoff policy and a small state machine to track soft vs hard consent failures and escalate only after repeated failures. The backoff respects per-tenant residency profiles and per-region rate limits.
- service/rbac: add operator_fence middleware which consults attribute-bound RBAC rules and enforces timebound operator assertions for zone-sensitive endpoints.
- api/audit: emit "residency.violation.mitigated" events when we take fallback paths, include a digestable proof blob and KMS attempt counters; audit writer tags events as "non-blocking" or "blocking".
- docs/security: add residency-backoff.md describing operator behavior, expected signals, and migration steps.
- tests: add integration tests to simulate intermittent KMS consent failures and assert the mitigator preserves SLA for read-only flows while preventing unsafe writes.

Design notes:
- Backoff parameters are configurable via k8s ConfigMap (defaults are conservative). We prefer to record and expose metrics (kms.consent.retries, kms.consent.backoff_seconds, residency.mitigations) rather than fail fast for multi-tenant hosts.
- The mitigator chooses a fallback that either routes to a region-allowed compatible model variant or returns a controlled 409 with an audit link when the action cannot be safely completed.
- Operator Fence is based on RBAC v2 attribute bindings: operator-scope tokens must include an "operator_scope" claim and be time-limited; middleware denies operator-scoped POST/PUTs without this claim.

Checklist:
- [x] Backoff state machine implemented and feature-flagged
- [x] RBAC operator fence middleware + tests
- [x] Audit enrichments for mitigations
- [x] Config & k8s patch for rollout
- [x] Integration tests covering read/write permutations and multi-tenant behavior
- [x] Docs and migration notes

Testing and validation:
- Local unit tests added for consent backoff logic and RBAC checks (run: make test/service).
- Integration CI stage simulates 30% KMS consent failure with ramping and verifies mitigator reduces hard rejects by >90% for read flows and properly surfaces blocking writes.
- Staging rollout validated against a tenant with geo-locked KMS; smoke tests passed.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to staging behind feature flag for 48h and monitor metrics: kms.consent.retries, residency.mitigations, api.error.5xx.
2) Canary rollout to 10% of hosts with traffic shaping for region-sensitive tenants.
3) Full roll when metrics show <1% increase in 4xx/5xx and mitigations are exercised.

Security considerations:
- The mitigator is intentionally conservative: it will not fall back for actions tagged as "must-not-migrate" in the data classification table.
- All mitigated events include a non-repudiable audit payload that contains KMS attempt timestamps and operator token fingerprint when applicable.
- Operator Fence reduces blast radius by requiring explicit operator scope assertions for configuration endpoints.

Related: Linear ENG-12849 implements the mitigation E2E design; SEC-4021 tracked the operator fence requirement. SUP-9876 is a customer ticket that motivated the work.

If tenant-specific overrides are needed, update tenancy API whitelist and then post the override via admin API. Monitor metrics kms.consent.retries and residency.mitigations for 48h.
notes: This PR reduces incident noise from transient KMS consent failures by preferring recorded mitigations + audit over hard rejects. Operator fence is an incremental safety control and should be extended to other region-sensitive endpoints in follow-up PRs (ENG-12910).
